entries.english: To all who see or hear this present charter, I, Konrad von Esserswil, citizen of Arbon, make known and openly acknowledge that the venerable lords, the provost and chapter of canons of the collegiate church of Saint Stephen in Constance, had brought certain disputes against me concerning the Vogtei over the village of Salmsach, which I purchased from Egelolf von Rosenberg. The people and property of that village, as regards fines and escheats, belong by hereditary right to those lords, their church, and the chapter of Saint Stephen. I have amicably and peaceably settled these disputes with them as follows. They and their officials and church have the right and power to judge matters concerning their own people and property, whether held in freehold or as fiefs, and whether the people are serfs or free. But because jurisdiction and ban rights belong to me by virtue of the Vogtei, I, or whoever is Vogt at the time, may judge cases concerning free people. Any fines imposed in such cases shall be divided: I, or the Vogt, may take one half, if we wish, and the other half shall go to the lords of Saint Stephen. Since jurisdiction and ban rights belong to me, I shall exercise them with restraint, as befits my honor and for which I wish to answer to God. I have also stated that the lord von Rosenberg granted me the same Vogtei with the right that I should succeed him as Vogt over his people. The lords of Saint Stephen willingly grant me this, provided that I and my successors acknowledge, without evasion, the rents, taxes, and services owed to a Vogt, as written in their register. I and all my successors may also enjoy the fishing rights in the Aa, without prejudice, as these rights belong to a Vogt and as other Vogts have enjoyed them without prejudice. It is also agreed and set down regarding the presentation to the church at Salmsach that the lords of Saint Stephen and a Vogt have had the following rights and custom: the lords shall present to the church in alternation. When they present once, at the next vacancy the Vogt shall present, and so we shall present alternately forever. Although it is now the lords’ turn to present to that church as soon as it falls vacant, they have graciously and willingly granted me and my heirs the right to make the next presentation as soon as the church becomes vacant, to compensate me for the expense and loss I incurred in purchasing the Vogtei because von Rosenberg had captured some of their people. After I and my heirs have made that presentation, I and my heirs and successors may again present to the church, when it next falls vacant, by our own right. When we have thus made these two presentations consecutively, as stipulated above, the lords of Saint Stephen shall make the next presentation and I and my heirs and successors the one after that; thereafter they and their church and successors, and I and my heirs and successors, shall continue to make presentations in this stated alternation forever, plainly and without deceit or malice. The lords of Saint Stephen have also expressly reserved for themselves, their church, and all their successors that these agreements shall not impair or damage any of their rights in their other courts, or concerning their other people and property. As true and open proof and lasting security for everything stated above, I, the aforesaid Konrad von Esserswil, give to the lords of Saint Stephen in Constance and their chapter, on behalf of myself, all my heirs, and successors, this charter sealed with my own seal, which I have openly attached. This was done and this charter was issued at Constance on the Friday before Saint Matthias the Apostle’s Day, in the year 1382. Seal: Damaged seal, 2.7 cm in diameter; its partly legible legend reads “+S.CV...ADI.DCI.ESSRISWILL.”
